title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.158). S/T is a morphism of schemes. E is an O_S-module with a stratification, equivalently an integrable connection. d^0_E : E -> E⊗Ω^1_{S/T} is the associated first-order differential operator, and E' -> E is a submodule. The previous page defines two kinds of 'Picard-Fuchs data'. (i) μ_D is attached to a differential operator D : E'' -> F, where E'' is a quotient. (ii) ν_Δ(P', d_{P'}) ∈ Γ(S,F) is attached to a differential operator Δ : E⊗Ω^1_{S/T} -> F with Δ∘d^0_E∘u = 0 on E'. The previous page also states ν_Δ = μ_D for D induced by D_0 = Δ∘d^0_E.

This page argues that in the favourable case (S/T of characteristic 0, Ω_{S/T} flat, implicitly S/T smooth) the μ_D can be expressed through the ν_Δ. It suffices that, for S affine, every relevant D is of the form Δ∘d^0_E.

This is stated as a Lemma, flagged as a special case of a much more general fact on differential operators. A differential operator D : E -> F corresponds to an O_S-linear map P^∞_{S/T}(E) -> F. Suppose this map vanishes on the submodule generated by δ(E), the 'horizontal' part coming from the stratification. Then D is exactly of the form Δ∘d^0_E with Δ : E⊗Ω^1_{S/T} -> F a differential operator. The indeterminacy in Δ is again given by differential operators Δ' : E⊗Ω^1 -> F, presumably those killed by composition with d^0_E. In char 0 these should be the operators of the form Δ''∘d^1_E.

In modern terms, this is exactness at the first two places of the linearized de Rham complex P^∞(E) -> P^∞(E⊗Ω^1) -> P^∞(E⊗Ω^2) of a module with integrable connection. That complex resolves E, by the Poincaré lemma for the linearization. Dually, it is the Spencer resolution D_{S/T}⊗Ω^•-dual ⊗E -> E of the D-module E. Applying Hom_{diff}(-,F) shows that the differential operators vanishing on horizontal data are exactly those factoring through d^0_E. The lemma serves to identify Grothendieck's two constructions of Picard-Fuchs operators: 'periods' ν_Δ via de Rham classes versus operators μ_D.
errors: 'Ω_{S/T} plat' alone is not enough for the lemma in general. One needs S/T smooth (or at least differentially smooth with Ω locally free of finite type), so that the linearized de Rham complex is exact (Poincaré lemma). Grothendieck presumably intends smoothness, as in the surrounding text.

The description of the indeterminacy is garbled or incomplete on the page (a crossed-out 'Δ∘d^0_E, E⊗Ω' followed by 'Δ' : E⊗Ω → F op diff'). The correct statement should be: Δ is determined up to operators Δ' with Δ'∘d^0_E = 0, i.e. Δ' = Δ''∘d^1_E in char 0. No proof is given; the margin of the previous page also says 'faire la vérification'.

ideas.what: Differential operators E->F annihilating the horizontal part are exactly those factoring as Δ∘d^0_E, with indeterminacy given by the next differential
ideas.modern_name: Exactness of the linearized de Rham complex / Spencer resolution of a D-module (Poincaré lemma for P^∞)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Spencer, Malgrange (analytic); Berthelot (linearization of differential operators, Cohomologie cristalline 1974); Katz-Oda; Grothendieck's crystalline ideas
ideas.where_published: Ideas around P^∞ and stratifications appear in EGA IV §16 and in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968); the specific lemma is not known to me in print by Grothendieck

ideas.what: Comparison of two definitions of Picard-Fuchs operators (μ_D vs ν_Δ) via this lemma
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic Picard-Fuchs equations from the Gauss-Manin connection (Katz-Oda, Katz 'Nilpotent connections')

deep.surprise_reason: A standard lemma (Spencer/linearized de Rham exactness in char 0) is used to identify two formulations of Picard-Fuchs operators. The material is careful but well within the Katz-Oda/Berthelot literature, and no new result or connection appears.
